title: ACTOR’S CUT: LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS
location: Morris Performing Arts Center | 211 N Michigan St | South Bend, 46601
description: Join us for the Actor’s Cut screening of "Little Shop of Horrors" to celebrate its 40th anniversary, hosted by Ellen Greene, the original Audrey from the iconic stage musical and beloved film adaptation. This special event features a rare appearance by Greene, along with exclusive meet-and-greet packages that include signed memorabilia and photo opportunities. "Little Shop of Horrors," directed by Frank Oz, is a cult-classic sci-fi musical comedy about Seymour Krelborn, a nerdy florist who nurtures a man-eating plant named Audrey II. As the plant's fame grows, it demands human sacrifices, putting Seymour’s love for coworker Audrey at risk. Don’t miss this unforgettable experience!

title: FILM: "FANTASIA" (1940)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center
description: Professor Pfinklepfunder's $1 Sunday Films Directed by James Algar, Samuel Armstrong, Ford Beebe Jr., et al. With Leopold Stokowski, Deems Taylor Rated G, 124 minutes An anomaly in the canon of Disney animated features, Fantasia holds a special place in many hearts and memories for its vibrant colors and, at times, plotless abstract pieces. Composed of eight different segments featuring classical music, the anthology of animated shorts act as their own music videos of sorts—an odd way for Mickey Mouse to star in his first feature film, but a timeless example copied by many on how animation and music can be woven into inspiration. GET TICKETS *Sponsored by the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Classic Cinema.

description: Browning Cinema New at the Browning Directed by Boots Riley With Keke Palmer, LaKeith Stanfield, Demi Moore Rated R, 113 minutes, DCP In English and Mandarin with English subtitles The latest film written and directed by Boots Riley, one of the most singular and creative brains in the business, explodes with such abundant color and trenchant commentary with such innovation that it feels like Jacques Tati is back on the playground, leading us all to a good time while at school. title: LECTURE—"AMERICAN ODYSSEY: WHAT AN ANCIENT STORY REVEALS ABOUT OUR DIVIDED SOULS"
location: University of Notre Dame
description: The ancient story of The Odyssey addresses fundamentally human questions of home, ambition, vengeance, and mercy. Yet as political philosopher Patrick Deneen reveals, it is also the most American of classical texts. Like Odysseus, the American identity is defined by a core tension: a simultaneous commitment to the comfort of home and the drive to leave it behind. In this compelling presentation, Deneen uses the lens of Western inheritance to unpack the divided soul of the American character. Arriving alongside the U. S. semi-quincentennial, his book offers a timely look at how an ancient Greek epic continues to shape our greatest stories, our cultural politics, and our national identity today. We will begin our evening with Prof. Deneen with book sales and signing at 6:15 p.m. ET in the atrium of the Eck Visitors Center. Following the conclusion of Prof. Deneen's remarks at 8:15 p.m., all event attendees are welcome to join us for a light reception. Patrick J. Deneen holds a B. A. in English literature and a Ph. D. in political science from Rutgers University. From 1995–97 he was speechwriter and special advisor to the director of the United States Information Agency. From 1997–2005 he was assistant professor of politics at Princeton University. From 2005–2012 he was the Tsakopoulos-Kounalakis Associate Professor of Government at Georgetown University, before joining the faculty of Notre Dame in fall 2012. He is the author and editor of several books and numerous articles and reviews and has delivered invited lectures around the world. Deneen was awarded the APSA's Leo Strauss Award for Best Dissertation in Political Theory in 1995, and an honorable mention for the APSA's Best First Book Award in 2000. He has been awarded research fellowships from Princeton University, Earhart Foundation, and the Institute for Advanced Study at the University of Virginia. His teaching and writing interests focus on the history of political thought, American political thought, liberalism, conservatism, and constitutionalism. His widely-discussed 2018 book, Why Liberalism Failed, has been translated into over twenty languages and was praised by former President Barack Obama. Originally published at constudies.nd.edu.

title: MERRIMANS’ PLAYHOUSE@THE RACLIN MURPHY MUSEUM – ABRAM COLLIER NONET
location: Raclin Murphy Museum of Art | 100 Moose Krause Circle | Notre Dame, IN 46556
description:
Spend a summer evening grooving to jazz on the Hiler Family Terrace at the Raclin Murphy Museum. Bring your own blanket or lawn chair (limited seating will be available on the Terrace) and settle in for some great music. Ivan’s Cafe will have food available for purchase, and a cash bar will be available.

The Abram Collier Nonet is a collective of some of Chicago’s finest musicians, headed by vocalist and baritone saxophonist Abram Collier. In addition to Collier, the group includes: Millie Ahearn (trumpet), Neil Carson (alto saxophone/woodwinds), Roy McGrath (tenor saxophone/woodwinds), Pete Charles Isaac (trombone), Shanth Gopalswamy (guitar), Aval Stanley (piano), Jesse Lear (bass), and Joel Baer (drums).

The Abram Collier Nonet performs a variety of original, ensemble-exclusive arrangements, ranging from jazz standards and repertoire from the Great American Songbook to selections from modern pop music and video game soundtracks adapted for jazz ensemble. In addition, the group plays original compositions by Collier himself, traversing folk, traditional and modern pop, and jazz. Heavily inspired by singers such as Frank Sinatra, Michael Bublé, Nat “King” Cole, and Harry Connick Jr., Collier uses the nonet as a vehicle to breathe new life into timeless music while bringing a traditional sound to a new, younger audience.

Museum galleries will be open so you can explore the work of art paired with the performance.

title: RITUAL BREAKS (EX-MUTEMATH MEMBERS) WSG SUCRÉ AND DEEP AL BRINDLE
location: Stockroom East | 625 E Jefferson Blvd | South Bend, IN 46617
description:
Ritual Breaks is an indie-electronic, dance-rock outfit consisting of former MUTEMATH bandmates Darren King and Roy Mitchell-Cárdenas and multi-instrumentalist Cory Hale. Inspired by a sonic spectrum of 70s soul, Afrobeat and analog synth-pop, King and Hale began Ritual Breaks in 2025 as an experimental/instrumental collaboration. As the duo began incorporating vocal elements into their project, they enlisted Mitchell-Cárdenas to contribute guitar and bass parts as well. Soon later, he officially joined the band. Ritual Breaks plans to release new music throughout the rest of 2026, culminating with a full-length album in the Fall.

Supporting is indie-pop band Sucré, formed by Eisley co-founder/vocalist Stacy King and her producer husband Darren, and LA-based, fashion-forward, electronic-pop duo Deep AL Brindle.

title: THE CHRISTOPHERS (2025)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Select a DateBrowning Cinema New at the Browning Directed by Steven Soderbergh With Ian McKellen, Michaela Coel, James Corden Rated R, 100 minutes, DCP Steven Soderbergh and Ian McKellen, two guys with zillions of credits to their filmographies, team up with the brilliant but lesser seen Miachaela Coel (I May Destroy You, Chewing Gum) in this lively black comedy. A mainstay of the London art scene since his starry breakout in the creative explosion of the 1960's, Julian Sklar (McKellen) has drifted into a cluttered, self-imposed seclusion. His two estranged children (James Corden, Jessica Gunning) enlist Lori (Coel) , a young painter and sometime-forger, to pose as a prospective assistant and gain access to a fabled series of unfinished canvases Julian has buried deep in his home studio, in a deceptive bid to secure an inheritance for themselves.

location: Indiana University South Bend Civil Rights Heritage Center | 1040 W Washington St | South Bend, IN 46601
description:
The Poetry Den isn't just a space; it’s a current, a monthly surge of voices, both sharing and listening, searching for something beautiful.

Pam Blair begins each gathering with an open mic, offering a stage to anyone who wants to share. It’s a place where words connect us, where the rhythm of shared experience echoes in every line. Next, a featured artist steps in, bringing a fresh perspective, a new story, and a captivating invitation to be present.

Find your voice at the Poetry Den, where stories connect and new perspectives bloom.

More information at crhc.iusb.edu.
